title: Derived scalar restriction has the balanced tensor-of-counits lax structure
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in a coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories and localizations $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and exact scalar restriction $s:\operatorname{Mod}_S\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$, with its termwise localization $V=D(s)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the signed direct-sum total tensor of complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Use the native derived tensor and lax localization maps
$$\lambda_{R;P,Q}:Q_RP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_RQ\longrightarrow Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$$
of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], and the analogous $\lambda_S$. Write $\kappa_P:VQ_SP\simeq Q_RsP$ for the canonical exact-localization comparison. Let $E=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-\dashv V$ be the canonical derived scalar adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], with counit $\epsilon$, and equip $E$ with the canonical strong monoidal pullback comparisons $t_{X,Y}:E(X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Y)\simeq EX\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}EY$ and $e:E(R[0])\simeq S[0]$ [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], applied to the identity geometric morphism with structural ring map $\varphi$.

Define $\sigma_{A,B}:VA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}VB\to V(A\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B)$ to be the adjoint transpose of $(\epsilon_A\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_B)\circ t_{VA,VB}$, and define $\sigma_0$ as the transpose of $e$ [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates]. Let $\gamma_{P,Q}:\operatorname{Tot}(sP\otimes_RsQ)\to s\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_SQ)$ be the chain map whose component on each $(p,q)$ summand is the balanced sheaf map sending every generalized pure tensor $x\otimes_Ry$ to $x\otimes_Sy$.

For every pair of complexes $P,Q$ of $S$-modules,
$$V(\lambda_{S;P,Q})\circ\sigma_{Q_SP,Q_SQ}
=\kappa_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_SQ)}^{-1}\circ Q_R(\gamma_{P,Q})\circ\lambda_{R;sP,sQ}\circ(\kappa_P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa_Q).$$
Moreover $\sigma_0$ is the actual degree-zero ring map $\varphi:R[0]\to V(S[0])$, under the regular-unit identifications. The family $\sigma$ is uniquely determined by this equation already on pairs of flat-term K-flat $S$-complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. It respects the fixed signed integer tensor/shift comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent]. These conclusions require no flatness of $\varphi$, no boundedness, and no K-flatness of $sP$ or $sQ$ over $R$; the map $\lambda_{R;sP,sQ}$ is not asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: For module sheaves $M,N$ over $S$, the pairing $(x,y)\mapsto x\otimes_Sy$ with values in $s(M\otimes_SN)$ is $R$-bilinear: $\varphi(r)x\otimes_Sy=x\otimes_S\varphi(r)y$. The sheaf tensor universal property therefore gives its unique map $sM\otimes_RsN\to s(M\otimes_SN)$. Map each $(p,q)$ summand into $s\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_SQ)$ and use the coproduct universal property to obtain $\gamma_{P,Q}$. Both composites with the differentials send $x\otimes_Ry$ to $dx\otimes_Sy+(-1)^p x\otimes_Sdy$, so this is a chain map. Bilinearity, the sheaf universal property and the coproduct inclusions also show naturality for chain maps in both variables. These arguments use generalized sections and sheafification, not a sectionwise formula for all sections of the sheaf tensor.

source.place: Tags 03CZ (sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); agent-written balanced-map construction

proof.text: Fix arbitrary $S$-complexes $P,Q$, and choose flat-term K-flat $R$-resolutions $a:U\to sP$, $b:W\to sQ$. Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_RW)$ and $H=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_SQ)$. The total-model theorem makes $T$ flat-term K-flat. Apply ringed pullback to the identity geometric morphism with structural map $\varphi$: the complexes $S\otimes_RU$, $S\otimes_RW$ and $S\otimes_RT$ are flat-term K-flat over $S$. Write $c_U:E(Q_RU)\simeq Q_S(S\otimes_RU)$, and likewise $c_W,c_T$, for the canonical computations. The specified tensor comparison $t$ on these models is the localization of the ordinary comparison $S\otimes_RT\simeq\operatorname{Tot}((S\otimes_RU)\otimes_S(S\otimes_RW))$. This is precisely the representative-normalized canonical comparison, not an arbitrary strong monoidal structure. The native $\lambda_R$ at $(U,W)$ and $\lambda_S$ at the extended pair are invertible. No such claim has been made for $(sP,sQ)$.

Define $i=\kappa_P^{-1}Q_R(a)$, $j=\kappa_Q^{-1}Q_R(b)$ and the isomorphism $h=(i\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}j)\lambda_{R;U,W}^{-1}:Q_RT\to VQ_SP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}VQ_SQ$. Write $f=V(\lambda_{S;P,Q})\sigma_{Q_SP,Q_SQ}$. The defining adjunct formula for $\sigma$, followed by naturality of the adjunction counit along $\lambda_S$, gives
$$f^\flat=\lambda_{S;P,Q}(\epsilon_{Q_SP}\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_{Q_SQ})t_{VQ_SP,VQ_SQ}.$$
Consequently, naturality of $t$ gives
$$(fh)^\flat=\lambda_{S;P,Q}\bigl((\epsilon_{Q_SP}E(i))\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}(\epsilon_{Q_SQ}E(j))\bigr)t_{Q_RU,Q_RW}E(\lambda_{R;U,W}^{-1}).$$
Here $q^\flat=\epsilon\circ E(q)$. These identities are just the Hom bijection and naturality; they do not require a tensor comparison involving restricted complexes to be invertible.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 07A4; agent-written expansion of the specified adjunction transpose

proof.text:
The canonical coefficient adjunction on representatives says that $\epsilon_{Q_SP}E(i)$ is $Q_S(A)c_U$, where $A:S\otimes_RU\to P$ sends $s\otimes u\mapsto s\,a(u)$; similarly $B:S\otimes_RW\to Q$ represents $\epsilon_{Q_SQ}E(j)$. The normalized adjunction is the derived ordinary extension/restriction adjunction in the statement; moving the degree-zero scalar factor from right to left introduces no sign. Substitute these formulas into step 3. Naturality of $\lambda_S$ moves $Q_S(A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_S(B)$ through $\lambda_S$. The representative formula for $t$ in step 2 then shows that $(fh)^\flat=Q_S(m)c_T$, where
$$m:S\otimes_RT\to H,\qquad s\otimes(u\otimes w)\longmapsto (s\,a(u))\otimes_S b(w).$$
Indeed the ordinary tensor comparison sends $s\otimes(u\otimes w)$ to $(s\otimes u)\otimes_S(1\otimes w)$; applying $A\otimes B$ gives exactly this formula. Equality follows first on generalized pure tensors and then on the total coproduct inclusions. Apply the same normalized Hom formula to $T$: $Q_S(m)c_T$ has adjunct $\kappa_H^{-1}Q_R(g)$, where $g:T\to sH$ is $u\otimes w\mapsto a(u)\otimes_S b(w)$.

Denote the proposed right side in the item by $r$. Naturality of the native lax localization map gives
$$\lambda_{R;sP,sQ}(Q_R(a)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(b))=Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes_Rb)\lambda_{R;U,W}.$$
After composing with $h$, its invertible $\lambda_{R;U,W}$ factors cancel and the $\kappa_P,\kappa_Q$ factors cancel against those in $i,j$. Hence
$$rh=\kappa_H^{-1}Q_R(\gamma_{P,Q}\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes_Rb))=\kappa_H^{-1}Q_R(g).$$
Step 4 and injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection give $fh=rh$. Cancel the isomorphism $h$ to obtain the required equation for the original arbitrary $P,Q$. This calculation only cancels $\lambda_R$ on the chosen resolving pair $(U,W)$; $\lambda_{R;sP,sQ}$ remains a morphism throughout.

proof.text: The complex $R[0]$ is flat-term K-flat: tensoring with it is the identity via the regular unitor, and therefore preserves every acyclic complex. The canonical unit comparison $e$ is represented by $S\otimes_RR\to S$, $s\otimes r\mapsto s\varphi(r)$, as prescribed by the regular-unit pullback identification. By the normalized coefficient adjunction, its transpose is represented by $R\to sS$, $r\mapsto1\otimes r\mapsto\varphi(r)$. By definition this transpose is $\sigma_0$. Thus it is the actual coefficient map in degree zero, including its scalar action, not just a morphism abstractly isomorphic to it.

If $P,Q$ are flat-term K-flat over $S$, $\lambda_{S;P,Q}$ is invertible, and so is its image under $V$. The displayed equation therefore fixes $\sigma_{Q_SP,Q_SQ}$ uniquely, even though the right side contains a possibly noninvertible $\lambda_{R;sP,sQ}$. For any other natural family satisfying these equations, use the resolving-localization determination theorem over $S$, with the two bifunctors $(A,B)\mapsto VA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}VB$ and $(A,B)\mapsto V(A\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B)$. Equality on these resolving pairs implies equality everywhere. Thus the uniqueness assertion is uniqueness as a natural tensor comparison, as for the lax structure in the statement.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 0FPT; resolving localization and cancellation

proof.text: For the signed shift assertion first take $P,Q$ flat-term K-flat over $S$ and the $R$-resolutions $a,b$ of step 2. For a first-variable shift use $U[n]\to s(P[n])$, and for a second-variable shift use $W[n]\to s(Q[n])$. These remain flat-term K-flat: terms are reindexed, and tensoring with a shifted complex is the shifted tensor up to the stated signed chain isomorphism, so still takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. In the formula $g(u\otimes w)=a(u)\otimes_Sb(w)$ of step 4, extracting the first shift is unsigned on both sides; extracting the second multiplies both sides on the $(p,q)$ summand by $(-1)^{np}$. The termwise comparison $\kappa$ commutes with shifts. The fixed resolving tensor comparisons over $R$ and $S$ commute with these chain shifts by the derived shift-descent theorem. Thus the shift squares for $fh$ and $rh$ agree with the prescribed ones; cancel $h$ and $V(\lambda_S)$ to obtain both shift squares for $\sigma$ on resolving $S$-pairs. Resolving-localization determination extends these equalities to all derived objects. The mixed sign is the same $(-1)^{ab}$ on both sides, with no permutation of factors. Neither this step nor the normalization calculation uses boundedness or flatness of $\varphi$.

Tot is flat-term K-flat by lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model. Steps 3-5: I recomputed (fh)^flat = lambda_S(QA tensor QB)lambda_S^-1 Q(c_ord)c_T = Q_S(m)c_T, and rh = kappa^-1 Q(gamma Tot(a tensor b)) = kappa^-1 Q(g), whose adjunct is m. So fh = rh, and only lambda_{R;U,W} is cancelled. Step 6: e is s tensor r -> s phi(r), and its transpose under the normalized unit is phi. Step 7: lambda_S is invertible on flat-term K-flat S-pairs, and the determination clause of lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent gives uniqueness as a natural family.
